read.title: Reading
read.noFindings: No abnormal findings: this is what normal looks like.
read.community: Clues are teaching notes reviewed by the community. Spot a mistake? Report it.
note.rate: Count the QRS complexes on the 10-second rhythm strip and multiply by 6, or divide 300 by the number of big squares between two R waves.
note.rhythm: Sinus rhythm conducts 1:1: an upright P in II, then a QRS, every time. 'No' when P waves are missing (AF, flutter, SVT), when some P waves are not conducted (2nd- and 3rd-degree block), or when beats start in the ventricle (PVCs, paced beats).
note.axis: Use I and II: both positive = normal (−30° to +90°); I positive but II negative = left (< −30°); I negative and aVF positive = right (> +90°).
note.pr: From the start of P to the start of QRS: 3–5 small squares (120–200 ms). Longer with every P conducted = first-degree AV block; shorter = think pre-excitation.
note.qrs: Under 3 small squares (< 120 ms) is narrow. Wide means the ventricles are activated abnormally: bundle branch block, ventricular beats, pacing or pre-excitation.
note.qt: Quick check: the T wave should end before the midpoint between two R waves. QTc above 450 ms (men) or 460 ms (women) is long.
note.st: Compare the segment after the QRS with the baseline before P. Elevation in two neighbouring leads suggests injury; check the opposite leads for reciprocal depression.
learn.question.rhythm: Is every P wave followed by a QRS, and every QRS preceded by its own P wave?
learn.question.qrs: Is the QRS narrow or wide?

heart.cap.rest: Rest: every cell is polarised and no current flows, so the line is flat.
heart.cap.P: P wave: the impulse from the SA node spreads through both atria.
heart.cap.P.retro: Retrograde P: the atria are activated backwards, from below.
heart.cap.P.flutter: Flutter wave: the front is on its way round the tricuspid ring.
heart.cap.P.af: Fibrillation: small wavelets wander through the atria; there is no organised P wave.
heart.cap.AV: AV node delay: too little tissue is active to show, so the PR segment is flat.
heart.cap.blocked: Blocked: this impulse doesn't get through to the ventricles.
heart.cap.pre: Delta wave: the accessory pathway starts the ventricle early, through slow ordinary muscle.
heart.cap.QRS: QRS: the ventricles depolarise, septum first, then both walls from inside out.
heart.cap.QRS.ventricular: Wide QRS: this beat starts in ventricular muscle and spreads slowly, cell to cell.
heart.cap.QRS.junction: Junctional escape: it starts just below the block and uses the normal conduction system, so the QRS is narrow.
heart.cap.ST: ST segment: the whole ventricle is depolarised (plateau). No voltage difference, so the line is flat.
heart.cap.reentry.flutter: Flutter circuit: the front is crossing the slow isthmus; little tissue is active.
heart.cap.reentry.avnrt: Re-entry in the AV node: down the slow pathway, back up the fast one.
heart.cap.reentry.avrt: Re-entry: down the AV node, back up the accessory pathway.
heart.cap.reentry.vt: Re-entry round the scar: each lap leaves through the same exit.
